Algebra 1 | Quarter 2 | Unit 4: Linear Equations and Functions

E(d): Function Notation on the Trail

What does E(500) = 1,640 mean?

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 8–9
Topic
Function Notation
Standards
HSF-IF.A.1, HSF-IF.A.2, HSF-IF.B.4

Students decide whether a relation is a function, evaluate functions in f(x) notation, solve f(x) = c, and interpret statements like E(500) = 1640 in context.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Decide whether a relation is a function from a table, a set of pairs or a graph.
  • Evaluate functions written in f(x) notation.
  • Solve equations of the form f(x) = c.
  • Interpret function notation in a real context.

3Essential question

Why do mathematicians give functions names, and what does a statement like E(500) = 1640 tell a rider?

5MTB connection

A ride file is a set of functions of time: distance D(t), elevation E(t), speed S(t). At each moment there is exactly one value of each.

Function notation is how coaches and data apps talk about a ride precisely: S(30) = 24 means “24 km/h at 30 minutes”.

The mathOn the trail
E(d)Elevation after d of trail
S(t)Speed at time t
Solving E(d) = cWhere on the trail you reach an elevation
Not a functionA trail that passes the same distance mark at two elevations (impossible)
